title: ## Mouse Jump preview window does not respond to mouse clicks in v0.101.2362.0
summary: The version-controlled Mouse Jump click regression is now also confirmed on 0.102.3001; reproduce input delivery versus coordinate mapping.

evidence: The original report supplies a repeatable preview-click failure on 0.101.2362.0 and a working 0.100.2 control on the same machine and settings.
Its Windows 11 25H2 configuration has a mirrored display pair plus a display to the right. The preview opens but left clicks neither move the pointer nor dismiss it.
A new October 28 reply independently confirms persistence on 0.102.3001.0; asking merely to try that version is now obsolete.
The attached Mouse Jump log is from the working 0.100.2 baseline and records successful target-coordinate handling; it does not trace the failing WinUI preview.
Read the full report and new confirmation and independently inspected the supplied archive, separating working-baseline logs from failing-version evidence.

Current PreviewWindow.xaml.cs::PreviewImage_PointerPressed filters mouse devices, reads a point relative to the image, applies a DPI ratio, searches screen bounds and returns without hiding the window when no layout matches.
Focused history locates the WinUI migration in #48393. This is a plausible regression boundary, not proof that its DPI transform is wrong.
The earlier focused investigation identified a center-click UI test but no mirrored-topology regression case; a single-display click test does not cover this report.
Bounded issue/PR/fork searches and timeline show no exact covering implementation or assignee. Adjacent Mouse Jump library PRs are not evidence of a shipped click fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Route a bounded full-design investigation after locating the first divergent click-path branch; preserve the working-baseline control.
judgment.rationale: The public report already provides topology, steps, a working baseline and a latest-version confirmation. The evidence supports a focused maintainer reproduction, not another generic logs or version request.

fix_assessment.rationale: A conditional click-path correction is warranted for investigation; no concrete covering fix or fork implementation is established.

proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: WinUI input delivery or pointer-to-layout mapping rejects clicks before cursor movement; the early no-layout return fits the unchanged preview. The exact failed branch, and whether mirrored topology is necessary, are not established.
proposed_fixes.title: Mouse Jump click-path regression investigation
verification: Click the center and edges of every represented screen, confirming the intended physical pointer position and preview dismissal.
Compare mouse click with keyboard selection to isolate input delivery from layout generation.
Retest on a non-mirrored layout and on the reporter topology at 0.102.3001; do not claim success based only on the baseline log.

confidence.rationale: The source identifies a plausible boundary, but this pass did not reproduce the failing transition. The accompanying diagnostic action distinguishes competing explanations.

plan: Reproduce the supplied mirrored topology and compare the working baseline with the first failing and latest-confirmed versions.
Determine whether handler entry is missing, a mouse/button guard returns, or the transformed point misses all screen bounds.
Design the correction only for the confirmed input/coordinate boundary; retain genuine background-click and non-mouse semantics.
Add coverage for the mirrored pair, adjacent display and mixed-DPI layouts as applicable.

reproduce.expected_result: Every valid thumbnail click moves the pointer to the corresponding display location and dismisses the preview; mirrored layouts do not make all clicks inert.
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare 0.100.2, 0.101.2362.0 and 0.102.3001 on the same configuration.
setup: Use Windows 11 with three displays: duplicate displays 1 and 3, with display 2 to the right. Enable Mouse Jump and preserve its settings across comparisons.
Record display scaling for the reproduction; use the supplied topology first before varying it.
prerequisites: Use non-sensitive test data and preserve the original configuration before changing it.
steps: 2. Left-click the center and edges of each screen thumbnail; note whether the preview dismisses and the pointer moves.
3. Compare keyboard screen selection, then repeat with duplication disabled as a control.
4. In a maintainer diagnostic session, correlate handler entry, mouse/button state, DPI transform and screen-layout match for each failing click.
5. Repeat the same cases across the working, first-failing and latest-confirmed versions.
